newsitem.title: GREECE: ECU/DRACHMA BREAKS ABOVE 308 ON SHORT-COVERING.
newsitem.headline: ECU/DRACHMA BREAKS ABOVE 308 ON SHORT-COVERING.

text.p: The ecu garnered more strength against the drachma breaking through the 308 resistance to trade around 308.50/70 in late dealings on light short-covering by local players in the thin market, forex dealers said.

"Ecu/drachma has firmed trading around 308.50/70," a dealer at a forex bank said. "Some domestic players have opted for some ecu buying for drachmas in precautionary short-covering in the thin market with the central bank abstaining."
Many markets abroad are closed today for Easter holidays.

"I am curious to see how foreign players will react tomorrow when they come back to their desks and see ecu/drachma at these levels," the forex dealer said who pointed out that ecu/drachma was hovering around 307.20/30 in late dealings last Thursday.
He was echoing other traders who expressed concern over the sharp rise of the ecu against the drachma in the last few days from 305.64 on March 24 to 308.30 on March 31 at the fixing.
"We have hit some stop losses on the way up," said the dealer. "Some of them have to be strategic positions."
Dealers said the firmer ecu/drachma had not sparked forex outflows so far.

"The bottom line is a stronger ecu/drachma with no or very few forex outflows since the central bank announced its new market operations tools to drain excess liquidity from the interbank market," said another forex dealer.

The question is whether the central bank is willing to tolerate a higher ecu/drachma even with a negligile effect on excess liquidity from the forex side or wants a weaker drachma to help contain the current account deficit, the dealer said.

Bank of Greece said last Wednesday it would institute regular, weekly 14-day depo and repo tenders and an overnight depo facility bounded by rates of 11.90 percent and 9.90 percent to fine-tune liquidity. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
